title: Global work remains low-engagement and emotionally costly, while work location and regional context redistribute both agency and wellbeing
source_unit: Gallup, State of the Global Workplace 2026, global employee survey and regional comparisons
geography: Global; Gallup regional groupings and employee subgroups

denominator.unit: Gallup global employee survey respondents; report page does not headline one pooled analytic denominator

employee_engagement_2025.unit: percent of employees engaged at work in 2025

observations.method: Gallup global workplace engagement indicator with historical comparison from 2009 through 2025.
observations.uncertainty: Global averages conceal country, occupation, sector, contract, age and workplace-power differences; engagement is a survey construct, not a direct measure of productivity or job quality.
observations.subgroup: Employees worldwide, with the report also presenting gender, age, job-level, work-location and regional cuts.
observations.counterinterpretation: The post-peak decline may reflect changing expectations or survey composition as well as worsening work experience; low engagement does not imply uniform dissatisfaction or imminent exit.

denominator.unit: Gallup global employee survey respondents; report page does not headline one pooled analytic denominator

life_thriving.unit: percent of employees thriving in life

life_struggling.unit: percent of employees struggling in life

life_suffering.unit: percent of employees suffering in life

daily_stress.unit: percent experiencing a lot of stress the previous day

daily_loneliness.unit: percent experiencing loneliness a lot of the previous day

observations.method: Gallup life-evaluation and daily-emotion indicators linked to employee status and workplace comparisons.
observations.uncertainty: The measures are self-reported and cross-sectional at the annual level; they do not establish that work conditions cause life evaluation or daily emotion differences.
observations.subgroup: Employees worldwide, with comparisons by gender, age, job level, work location and region.
observations.counterinterpretation: Life wellbeing may be driven more by household, community, health or macroeconomic conditions than by the workplace itself; employee status is not a complete social position.

observations.period: 2025; engagement by work location and region

denominator.unit: Gallup global employee survey respondents in the applicable work-location and regional groups; exact analytic denominators not disclosed

engagement_exclusively_remote.unit: percent engaged among exclusively remote employees

engagement_onsite_nonremote.unit: percent engaged among on-site, non-remote-capable employees

engagement_us_canada.unit: percent engaged in the United States and Canada regional grouping

engagement_europe.unit: percent engaged in Europe regional grouping

observations.method: Cross-sectional comparison of employee engagement by work location and Gallup regional grouping.
observations.uncertainty: Work location is not randomly assigned and is entangled with occupation, income, autonomy, commuting constraints, sector and employer selection; regional groupings are broad.
observations.subgroup: Exclusively remote, hybrid, on-site remote-capable and on-site non-remote-capable employees; Gallup regional groupings.
observations.counterinterpretation: Remote-capable workers may begin with more autonomy, higher-status occupations and better job fit, so the location gradient cannot be read as a pure causal effect of remote work.

denominator.unit: Gallup global employee survey respondents in the applicable work-location groups; exact analytic denominators not disclosed

thriving_onsite_remote_capable.unit: percent thriving among on-site, remote-capable employees

thriving_exclusively_remote.unit: percent thriving among exclusively remote employees

daily_stress_hybrid.unit: percent experiencing significant daily stress among hybrid employees

daily_stress_exclusively_remote.unit: percent experiencing significant daily stress among exclusively remote employees

observations.method: Gallup comparison of life evaluation and daily stress across work-location categories.
observations.uncertainty: The work-location categories combine autonomy, commute, occupation, household setting and employer policy; these descriptive differences are not causal estimates.
observations.subgroup: Hybrid, exclusively remote, on-site remote-capable and on-site non-remote-capable employees.
observations.counterinterpretation: Hybrid work may support wellbeing for some workers while also adding coordination and boundary costs; aggregate thriving and stress can move together.

related_sources.claim: Official downloadable 2026 report used for retrieval verification and hash.
Official Gallup data summary with global, subgroup and regional workplace indicators.

boundary: This record adds a comparative work-and-wellbeing mechanism: global engagement remains low after a 2022–23 peak, emotional strain remains elevated, and work location and region correspond with markedly different engagement and wellbeing profiles. It is a repeated global survey and descriptive subgroup comparison, not a causal evaluation of remote or hybrid work, a respondent-level panel, a job-quality audit or proof that one work arrangement generalizes across occupations and countries.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Gallup 2026 global data summary and downloadable report were retrieved and reviewed for engagement, life evaluation, daily emotions, job climate, work-location and regional comparisons; the PDF was hashed.
